guidelines.detail: refines XML-06 (The validator (V-L1) rejects the name attribute on messageEventDefinition, which is a schema violation (V-L1-1 gives the line). The only documented guidelines near this are EVT-14 (messageRef placement) and XML-06 (general schema conformance). Neither forbids a name on messageEventDefinition, so the failure is not covered explicitly. The description record S3 does not bear on this error and is not)

new guideline (The reference has an explicit approval task on the approved branch of the 'Promotion approved?' gateway, then a parallel split and join around the finalization and compensation actions, and a separate non-approved end. The generated model lacks the approval task (M3), the compensation task (M2), the exclusive gateway for the non-approved outcome (M5), and the approved-branch flows (F8, F9), and it)

same as LRN-018 (The reference has a task "Transition into new role" (M1) before the end, but the generated model has an extra end event named after the transition (X2) and no task for it. Its end event's label is the only trace of the transition, which is why the label-similarity mismatches (P1) arise. The description ends with the employee transitioning into the new role (S6), so the transition is a described ac)

refines GW-04 (The description says the employee keeps working on skill enhancement while receiving feedback, so both branches must run and complete. Reference gateways M3, M4 and M5 place exclusive gateways around that split and join with no stated decision. An exclusive join would pass on each arriving branch instead of waiting for all of them, which breaks BPMN 2.0.2 semantics. GW-04 already requires parallel)

refines PROC-04 (The only difference the records support as a modeling choice is M2, the reference's exclusive gateway around the approval outcome and the transition into the new role. S5 states an approval decision that finalizes the promotion, and the not-approved branch ends the process separately. The parallel gateway omissions (M1, M3, M4, M5) are not learnable, since the description states no decision there )

rules_sent_back.instruction: When The description names a message that a process event sends or waits for, so the model needs a message event definition.: Place the event's name on the event element itself (or on a referenced bpmn:message element). On the bpmn:messageEventDefinition, set only its id and messageRef attributes, and never give it a name attribute, because the BPMN 2.0.2 XSD does not allow one.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description names a message that a process event sends or waits for, so the model needs a message event definition.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a review leads to an approval decision, that only the approved outcome is then carried out, and that the approved outcome consists of several actions that must all be done before the process moves on: Model the review as a task, and the approval decision as an exclusive gateway with a conditioned approved branch and a separate non-approved branch that ends in its own end event. On the approved branch, first place a task that carries out the approval, then open a parallel gateway that splits into one task per required action, and close those tasks with a matching parallel gateway join before the next step. Do not skip the approval task or route the approved actions directly from the decision gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a review leads to an approval decision, that only the approved outcome is then carried out, and that the approved outcome consists of several actions that must all be done before the process moves on

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the flow terminates in one of two alternative actions performed on the subject, with each action named in the description: Place an exclusive gateway at the point where the alternative is chosen. After each branch, model the named action as its own task, labeled with the action the description names, and connect that task to its own end event. Do not model an action only as an end event labeled with the resulting state, and do not merge the alternative action tasks into one task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the process ends once the subject is moved into a new state by a described transition, after a set of approved actions has been completed

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that work on one activity continues in parallel with another activity or feedback stream, and it states no condition, decision or criterion at the point where those concurrent branches split or rejoin: Model the split with a parallel gateway and close the concurrent branches with a matching parallel gateway that waits for all of them. Do not insert exclusive gateways at the split or join, and do not add condition labels to these branches. Use an exclusive gateway only where the description names a decision with alternative outcomes.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that work on one activity continues in parallel with another activity or feedback stream, and it states no condition, decision or criterion at the point where those concurrent branches split or rejoin

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a review or approval outcome that can be approved or not approved, where the approved outcome leads to a finalization activity and the not-approved outcome ends the process on a separate branch: Model the outcome as an exclusive decision gateway placed directly after the review activity, with one outgoing flow for each outcome. Give the not-approved flow its own terminal end event. Do not route the approved flow to a termination or a shared end before the finalization activity. Use an exclusive gateway only where the outcome selects one branch, and do not add it to parallel branches.
